An attribute keyed `format:name` is used as `name` when that format is the one being rendered, and dropped otherwise.

```markdown
::: {html:style="color: firebrick;" revealjs:style="color: deepskyblue;"}
Firebrick on a page, deep sky blue on a slide.
:::
```

::: {html:style="color: firebrick;" revealjs:style="color: deepskyblue;"}
Firebrick on a page, deep sky blue on a slide.
:::

`slide:` covers every HTML slide format at once, and `default:` supplies a value for the formats that name none.

```markdown
::: {default:style="color: grey;" html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
Rebecca purple in HTML, grey everywhere else.
:::
```

::: {default:style="color: grey;" html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
Rebecca purple in HTML, grey everywhere else.
:::

The prefix is the name of the format Quarto targets, so a custom format is written by its own name rather than the writer beneath it, and PDF is `latex:`.

Set `warn-on-drop` under `extensions.prism` to catch a mistyped prefix, which is otherwise indistinguishable from a format that is simply not active.

Full documentation: <https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-prism/>.
